correctness.rationale: Use factor rank, i.e. containment of the image words in the semigroup on a candidate basis, not the number of generators of the image subsemigroup itself. With n distinct two-letter images, choosing singleton basis letters S forces every image not internal to S to occur as a two-letter basis word. The minimum basis size is therefore min_S(n+|S|-e(S)); e(S)≤|S| is the pseudoforest condition. Equality of the total edge and vertex counts forces one cycle per component. A nonempty proper tight S gives a size-n mixed basis and two nonautomorphisms; conversely a factorization of a rank-preserving map uses all intermediate letters and yields such a mixed basis unless one factor is a permutation. A proper tight S exists exactly when a cycle omits a vertex. In particular the binary irreducible image set is just {ab,ba}. In the connected EGF the loop, double-edge and longer cycle terms are T, T²/2 and 2^(k−1)T^k/k; summing components via SET and assigning the distinct images to source letters gives the two n! factors. At rho=1/(2e), 1−2T~sqrt(2(1−z/rho)). The rooted tree series is convergent at rho and has positive consecutive coefficients, so |T|<1/2 at all other boundary points and the implicit function is regular there. Transfer and B_n/A_n=2^(n−1)/(n[z^n]F) give the frozen constant and exponent. An independent Hall incidence-assignment count gives 6,72,1274,29610 rank-preserving image sets for n=2–5; independent Lagrange coefficient extraction agrees through n=8.
residual_risks: Finite coefficient checks are corroboration, not the basis of the all-size proof. The final analytic continuation detail is made explicit here; aperiodicity is used for T along with the implicit equation, not as a general uniqueness theorem for singularities of arbitrary series.
